page: Microsoft Azure D32ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processors running on the x86_64 architecture with a clock speed of up to 4.5 GHz. It features 32 virtual CPUs derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The memory configuration totals 128.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU allocation. Local storage includes a bundled 1890 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes zero GPUs.

Benchmark results show notable single-thread processing capabilities. The instance scored 3753.87 in stress-ng single-core tests, placing it in the top tier. PassMark CPU extended instructions and encryption benchmarks scored strongly at 53395.54 and 40124.54 respectively, supported by hardware AVX-512 and cryptographic extensions. Multi-threaded stress-ng throughput registered at 60013.36, representing average tier scaling across its 32 threads. Memory benchmarks recorded an uncached read bandwidth of 101.21 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 67.44 GB/sec, alongside a strong PassMark memory score of 2908.92.

The inclusion of high-speed local NVMe storage combined with a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio provides practical cost efficiency for IO-intensive operations without requiring supplemental ephemeral block storage attachments. However, as a non-accelerated CPU instance without discrete GPUs, large-scale model training is impractical, though lightweight inference remains feasible. The configuration is best aligned with enterprise web applications, intermediate relational database servers, caching layers, and continuous integration pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D32ads_v7 is a general-purpose instance providing 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores via an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. Configured with 128.0 GB of memory adhering to a standard 1:4 core-to-RAM ratio, it bundles 1890 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage with zero discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier single-core performance alongside strong encryption and extended instruction execution via AVX-512 support. The balanced hardware design delivers solid resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for input-output heavy workloads that benefit from direct NVMe access. D32ads_v7 is well suited for relational databases, Redis caching layers, web serving platforms, and continuous integration build environments.
